newsitem.title: ITALY: Court awards Cecchi Gori Italy soccer rights.
newsitem.headline: Court awards Cecchi Gori Italy soccer rights.

text.p: A court ruled on Wednesday that the rights to broadcast Italian league soccer on regular television should go to media tycoon Vittorio Cecchi Gori rather than state broadcaster RAI.

The decision, which remains provisional pending a final verdict and evidence that Cecchi Gori has the funds to buy the rights, marked the latest round in a battle between the owner of Italy's two private TeleMonteCarlo channels and RAI.
This season's soccer -- covered by RAI -- is not subject to the ruling, which affects the next two seasons.
"It's a great triumph for our group, but we were sure that the law was on our side," said Luciano Luna, managing director of Cecchi Gori's Fiorentina soccer club.

Cecchi Gori Communications, the holding company of TeleMonteCarlo (TMC), TMC2 and VideoMusic channels, said in a statement that the Florence court had recognised "our true right and the bad actions of others".
"We have suffered a grave injury which has delayed our development and has deprived us of the rights to soccer for an entire season," the statement said.
It said Cecchi Gori Communications was seeking damages and was determined to carry out the best service for the 1997/98 and 1998/99 seasons covered by the rights purchased.
Cecchi Gori was awarded the television and radio rights at the end of February after he offered the soccer league 213.5 billion lire ($140 million) a year for exclusive coverage.
RAI offered only 185 billion lire ($121 million) in the secret auction and the prospect of losing the rights, which it has always held, sent shock waves through the company.
RAI, which is funded both by a licence fee and advertising, had argued that as a state-owned broadcaster it had a duty to the public to broadcast soccer.

However, Cecchi Gori's stations, whose signals can not be received throughout all of Italy, failed to deposit bank guarantees to cover the bid and in March offered to withdraw their offer "as a sign of responsibility".
In April, RAI said it had regained the rights after further discussions with the Milan-based soccer league.
But Cecchi Gori challenged the move and police impounded documents relating to the controversial auction.
The judge ruled that Cecchi Gori had until March 20, 1997, to present sureties of 213.5 billion lire ($140 million) requested by the league at the time of the original bidding.
It also ordered Cecchi Gori to pay 158 billion lire ($103 million) to the court as security by May 31, 1997.
The League said in a brief statement on Wednesday that it would "abide scrupulously" with the court ruling.
A Cecchi Gori spokesman told Reuters that the group was ready to meet its financial obligations.

The rights do not cover pay-per-view screening of Italian league soccer, broadcast in coded form, which belong to the Telepiu 2 channel. Neither do they cover matches played by the national team or European club competitions. $1=1520 lire
